100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On August 10, 1926, tensions escalated in the Middle East as British authorities clashed with Arab nationalists in Palestine, raising concerns over stability in the region. In the United States, the Ford Motor Company announced significant layoffs due to declining sales, signaling potential economic troubles ahead. Meanwhile, the world celebrated the opening of the 1926 Summer Olympics in Amsterdam, showcasing athletic prowess and international camaraderie despite ongoing global challenges.
